paragraphs: The Citan 109 CDI has been a key diesel variant in the Citan range since 2012, spanning two generations under one badge. Earlier models (W415, 2012 to 2021) use the K9K — a 1.5-litre diesel sourced from Renault and shared with the Kangoo of that era. From 2021, the W420-generation Citan 109 CDI switched to OM607 or OM608 engines, which are different units with their own specification. The engine code matters because the components, known wear patterns and rebuild specifics differ between them — which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every CITAN 109 CDI on the road.

cards.body: A 1.5-litre diesel fitted to the Citan 109 CDI from 2012 to 2021 across the W415 generation. Known for injector failure and EGR clogging — see the callout above. We replace injectors, EGR components and gaskets as standard on every K9K rebuild, along with timing chain components where worn.

compatibility.intro: Because the Citan 109 CDI spans distinct engines across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (M256) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic Citan quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
